title: Interleaved tensor suspension with its internal differential
statement:
Use smallness as in [def-weil-size-convention], tensor products as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and cochain shifts as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: $K[r]^q=K^{q+r}$ and $d_{K[r]}=(-1)^r d_K$. For $n\geq0$ let $K_0,\ldots,K_{n+1}$ be arbitrary cochain complexes of abelian groups. Let $E=\mathbf Z\varepsilon$ in degree $-1$ with zero differential. Put $V_n=K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n+1}$ and $W_n=K_0\otimes E\otimes K_1\otimes E\otimes\cdots\otimes K_n\otimes E\otimes K_{n+1}$, with the tensor differential $d(u\otimes v)=du\otimes v+(-1)^{|u|}u\otimes dv$ and direct-sum totalization. For homogeneous $x=a_0\otimes\cdots\otimes a_{n+1}$, the formula
$$\Phi_n(x)=(-1)^{\alpha_n(x)}a_0\otimes\varepsilon\otimes a_1\otimes\varepsilon\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n\otimes\varepsilon\otimes a_{n+1},\qquad \alpha_n(x)=n+\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(n+1-j)|a_j|$$
defines an isomorphism of cochain complexes $\Phi_n:V_n[n+1]\xrightarrow{\sim}W_n$, natural in degree-zero chain maps of all $K_j$. In particular $d_{W_n}\Phi_n=\Phi_n((-1)^{n+1}d_{V_n})$. The same formula defines the inverse by removing the generators and multiplying by the same sign; no flatness or boundedness of the $K_j$ is required.
